<unit id>.title: topic page name

_schema.next_action: one imperative sentence a fresh run can execute without any other context

_schema.ready_to_merge: boolean — true when the task is complete and the final cross-topic check is on main (under auto policy every unit is already merged)
_schema.merge_policy: auto | hold | direct — auto (default) merges every completed unit into main immediately; hold keeps one open PR for the task; direct pushes completed units to main without PRs

dg-iv.diagnosis: Diagnosis: the graph has a strong constant-rank/regular-level-set spine, but its global-theorem layer overclaims completeness. The Whitney page states a proper noncompact theorem while its formal proof only proves the compact case; it also falsely says smooth functions become polynomial restrictions. The topic attributes genericity of Morse functions to Sard alone, states an overbroad transversality openness claim, and contains several bridges that confuse detection with classification or require missing hypotheses. Proof audit must also eliminate abbreviated “similarly/clearly” cases and verify the quotient-property, figure-eight, Hopf, Sard, and projection arguments line by line. Target: organize the chapter around rank as first-order normal form data, then present embedded and immersed submanifolds as the parametric/implicit outputs of that normal form. Give fully typed local normal-form proofs, a reusable regular-value workflow with calibrated matrix-group examples, an honest coordinate-invariant measure-zero definition and complete Sard proof at the stated differentiability, and a Whitney page whose statement matches a complete compact/noncompact proof. Separate Sard, parametric transversality, and jet transversality; distinguish injective immersion, embedding, proper embedding, and initial submanifold; and make exercises train transitions among parametrizations, equations, tangent kernels/images, and genericity arguments.
dg-iv.notes: Diagnosis and target recorded. First rewrite checkpoint corrects the compact/general Whitney proof contract, a false cutoff inference in injectivity, the polynomial-restriction claim, and the hypotheses behind Morse/transversality genericity. Next: normal-form theorem proofs. Rank-theorem checkpoint expands the inverse calculation and corrects the overbroad algebraic-geometry Jacobian criterion by stating the expected-codimension caveat. Sard checkpoint corrects the vanishing-set filtration, zero-dimensional edge cases, hypersurface induction, and false claims that Sard alone yields slice transversality or Morse nondegeneracy. Local normal-form checkpoint types every Euclidean domain and shrinking, proves both converses by the chain rule, and corrects overclaims about bundle trivializations, covering lifts, metric flatness, and section embeddings. Regular-value checkpoint qualifies the constant-rank fibre statement, replaces metric-dependent perpendicular language by annihilators, types the Lie-subgroup inference, and separates quotient fibres from orbit-map constant rank. Submanifold-definition checkpoint clarifies the graph parametrization, gives a differentiable obstruction for corners, fixes the direction of the immersed-versus-subspace topology comparison, and qualifies canonicity relative to a chosen injective immersion. Example checkpoint replaces the circular Hopf-kernel dimension argument with a projective-chart computation, removes drafting leakage, distinguishes submersions from fibre bundles, corrects the orthogonal-group tangent-codomain explanation, and qualifies density of nonclosed subgroups. Final pass fixed the rank theorem’s disconnected-fibre gap by shrinking to product balls and integrating along fibres, repaired remaining map-typing and topology claims, and passed all four mechanical audits plus a 24-page link/exercise graph audit. All target gaps are closed; advanced noncompact Whitney variants are explicitly separated from the complete compact proof.

dg-v.diagnosis: Diagnosis: the graph is extensive but repeatedly substitutes slogans for hypotheses. The Hopf proof contains a circular rank-nullity argument; arbitrary one-parameter families are conflated with flows; submersions with fibre bundles; flowout charts with tubular neighbourhoods; and Sard-style genericity with transversality. Several flow and bracket pages use untyped local-domain compositions, omit the maximal-flow-domain logic, or state noncommutation remainders and sign conventions imprecisely. The straightening, commuting-flow, compact-support completeness, Reynolds transport, and Jacobi proofs require line-by-line review. Target: organize DG V around a vector field as both a derivation and an autonomous ODE, with the maximal flow as its local one-parameter action. Prove existence, uniqueness, smooth dependence, the group law, completeness criteria, straightening, bracket naturality/Jacobi, and the bracket–flow commutator relation with all domains and signs explicit. Separate local from global statements, distinguish arbitrary isotopies from flows, explain vertical/horizontal and Lie-derivative constructions without importing later bundle hypotheses, and use examples/exercises that move between coordinate ODEs, derivations, flows, pushforwards, and commutators.
dg-v.notes: Diagnosis and target recorded before content editing. First target gap: repair flow definitions and maximal-flow theorem, then audit bracket/commuting-flow calculus. Flow-definition checkpoint separates open total domains from open time slices, records maximal-domain translation, avoids assuming a Lie structure on Diff(M), distinguishes regular from singular orbit foliations, and separates isotopies from autonomous flows. Maximal-flow checkpoint replaces a circular openness proof by finite smooth-dependence compositions, types time-slice openness and inverse domains, repairs the uniform-time extension interval, and qualifies Hamiltonian/geodesic completeness claims. Bracket checkpoint fixes singular-set continuity, removes unsupported natural-operation and scalar-curvature claims, states two-parameter commutator remainders correctly, and restores hypotheses for torus actions and Liouville–Arnold. Final review corrected the flow-commutator order, removed drafting leakage, integrated Reynolds/Faraday into the concept and exercise maps, fixed Faraday orientation, and passed all mechanical plus 28-page graph audits. Every target gap is closed.

dg-vi.diagnosis: Diagnosis: the unit has a strong local-frame/cocycle spine but the cotangent-bundle proof loses control of transition-map conventions and contains explicit drafting corrections instead of a valid cocycle proof. The topic falsely says vector-field pushforward is legal exactly for diffeomorphisms, several section-to-bundle “fully faithful” statements need base-map and locality qualifications, and the punctured-plane angle discussion confuses arctan with a genuine branch. Exactness, reparametrization orientation, bundle gluing topology, Möbius nontriviality, and all inverse-transpose formulas require line-by-line review. Target: organize the chapter around vector bundles as locally free linear data glued by a GL(k)-cocycle, with precise equivalence among trivializations, frames, sections, and transition matrices. Construct dual/cotangent bundles with one fixed convention and prove pairing invariance and cocycles without index ambiguity; distinguish pullback of covectors from projectable pushforward of vectors; derive df, line integrals, exactness, periods, and simply-connected path independence with oriented reparametrizations and complete proofs. Exercises should move fluently among gluing matrices, frames, sections, dual transformations, and integral tests.
dg-vi.notes: Diagnosis and target recorded before content editing. First rewrite: rebuild cotangent transition maps with a single convention and remove drafting leakage. Cotangent checkpoint replaces contradictory index calculations with pairing-invariance proof, fixes (AB)^(-T) order and cocycle convention, and aligns the construction exercise. Contravariance checkpoint replaces the false diffeomorphism-only pushforward rule by F-related projectability, corrects angle branches on the punctured plane, and separates the 1-form exactness theorem from higher-degree magnetic potentials. Final review corrected base-map uniqueness, supplied a genuine non-covering map, qualified vector-field transport by F-relatedness, corrected frame-group action and zero-section dimension, and distinguished reparameterization invariance from dependence on an image set. All mechanical and 29-page graph audits pass.
